name: Dual-Use Regulation
evidence_rating: thin: annual Commission implementation reports with licensing and trade statistics; no evaluation of effects
summary: The recast export-control regime applies since September 2021. The Commission's annual implementation reports put dual-use exports at about 2.7% of EU exports (EUR 128 billion in 2020) and describe licensing activity, but licensing decisions are not public and no evaluation of the Regulation's effects exists.

indicators.objective: No monitoring indicators set in the proposal; assessed through the Commission's reports listed below

indicators.evidence: Dual-use exports about 2.7% of EU exports (EUR 128 billion, 2020); latest report covers 2024.

literature.citation: European Commission (2022), Report on the implementation of Regulation (EU) 2021/821 (2021), COM(2022) 434
literature.title: Report on the implementation of Regulation (EU) 2021/821 (2021)
literature.headline: Dual-use exports about 2.7% of EU exports, EUR 128 billion in 2020
literature.summary_plain: Dual-use items make up a small but significant share of EU exports.

literature.citation: European Commission (DG TRADE) (2026), Report from the Commission on the implementation of Regulation (EU) 2021/821 (annual report on dual-use export controls, 2024 data), COM(2026) 296, European Commission report
literature.title: Report from the Commission on the implementation of Regulation (EU) 2021/821 (annual report on dual-use export controls, 2024 data), COM(2026) 296
literature.method: aggregation of Member State licensing data under Art 26 of Regulation 2021/821
literature.outcomes: value of authorised dual-use exports; denials
literature.headline: Authorised dual-use exports were EUR 77.6bn in 2024 (up from EUR 71bn), about 3% of extra-EU goods exports. Member States denied 487 transactions on end-use security grounds.
literature.summary_plain: Official licensing statistics show how much dual-use trade is controlled and how often licences are refused, but not whether controls achieved their security aims or what they cost firms.
literature.quality: descriptive administrative data; no impact evaluation
literature.verified: publisher (Commission news) page read; full report not read

literature.citation: Versino, C. (2015), Dual-use trade figures and how they combine, JRC Technical Report (European Commission Joint Research Centre)
literature.title: Dual-use trade figures and how they combine
literature.venue: JRC Technical Report (European Commission Joint Research Centre)
literature.method: bounding estimate combining Member State licence data and Eurostat COMEXT export data
literature.outcomes: size of EU dual-use export sector
literature.headline: Estimates total intra- plus extra-EU dual-use export value at 'at most 3.3%' of total EU exports in 2013, about EUR 150bn. It was produced to give a method for assessing the trade impact of controls during the review of Regulation 428/2009.
literature.summary_plain: A Commission research report measured how big dual-use trade is (a few percent of EU exports) but did not measure the effect of controls.
